camss_without_iommu.truncation: data only in the first rows: the physically contiguous start of a scattered buffer (see correction), not a bandwidth limit
camss_without_iommu.correction: 2026-10-31 later: the 'truncation' was not bandwidth. Without an IOMMU, videobuf2-dma-sg buffers are scattered pages, and the VFE writes each frame linearly from the first segment's address. Only the physically contiguous start of the buffer receives data; the rest of the frame overwrites unrelated memory. A later no-IOMMU run with full-size frames crashed the kernel on a pointer made of CSID test-pattern bytes (0x07060504). No-IOMMU captures are unsafe: CAMSS on MSM8226 needs the VFE IOMMU (or contiguous buffers).
